text:
Dylan Brooks: hey all — need quick alignment on UI copy for Optimize quality gate failures + the override states. We’re getting inconsistent wording across Console (results panel vs apply modal). Can we settle on labels for: gate failed, override requested, override granted (time-bound), override denied?

Kenji Nakamura: yup. here’s what I have in the latest wire notes (very draft):
- FAILED: “Quality check failed” + “This change would degrade output quality beyond allowed thresholds.”
- OVERRIDE REQUESTED: “Override requested” + “Waiting for approval.”
- OVERRIDE GRANTED: “Override granted” + “Expires <date>.”
- OVERRIDE DENIED: “Override denied” + “This change can’t be applied.”
Open question: do we say “quality gate” explicitly everywhere or keep it human (“quality check”)?

Alicia Perez: +1 on consistency. I lean “Quality gate” in product surfaces since users see it in docs + audit logs. But in the inline warning, “quality check” is less scary.

Chloe Martin: for API -> UI mapping: backend is going to return gate_state + override_state (pending/granted/denied) + override_expires_at. If we use “quality check” in one place and “quality gate” in another, we should make sure we don’t mismatch with the audit log event names (those are “quality_gate_*”).

Aditya Rao: preference from PM side: call it “Quality gate” in the header, then use plain language in the explanation. Example:
Header: “Quality gate failed”
Body: “This optimization is blocked because it causes a measurable regression on our evaluation suite.”
Also important: we should avoid implying that overrides are automatic. “Override requested” needs to be explicit that it’s awaiting an approver.

Jordan Lee: +1. Also: we need to be careful that “Override granted” doesn’t read like the gate passed. It’s still failing; the override is an exception. Maybe we should literally show “Gate: Failed” and then “Exception: Approved (expires …)”.

Felix Schneider: from audit view, we’re planning to show both anyway (gate outcome + exception). If the main apply screen collapses that into one status pill, it gets confusing in exports.

Kenji Nakamura: ok so maybe the status structure is:
- Primary status line: “Gate: Failed” / “Gate: Passed”
- Secondary badge (only if relevant): “Exception: Requested” / “Exception: Approved (expires …)” / “Exception: Denied”
Copy in the panel can follow that.

Dylan Brooks: that works for me. But we also need the call-to-action button text for failures. Right now UI has “Request override” vs “Override this gate”. I’d like to avoid the second (sounds too easy).

Alicia Perez: button should be “Request exception” not “Request override” IMO. “Override” sounds like you’re bypassing safety; “exception” reads like policy.

Aditya Rao: we used “override” language in the policy doc and release notes draft. If we switch to “exception” in UI, we need to make sure docs don’t conflict. Maybe: UI uses “Request exception” and in small text: “Exception (override) requests require approval.”

Jada Williams: from approvals workflow side, “exception” maps better to the actual model: it’s time-bound and tied to an owner + reason code. “Override” is a verb, but in our system it’s an object.

Chloe Martin: implementation detail: we can expose both strings, but I’d rather not. Let’s pick one canonical term. If we choose “exception” in UI, I’ll confirm the API fields still say override_state but UI label can be “Exception”.

Jordan Lee: +1 on “exception” as user-facing, “override_*” internal is fine.

Kenji Nakamura: proposing final copy (v2):
Header (failure): “Quality gate failed”
Subtext: “This optimization is blocked because it regresses quality beyond the allowed threshold.”
Details link: “View evaluation results”
CTA (no exception): “Request exception”
If exception pending: show badge “Exception requested” + helper: “Awaiting approval from an authorized reviewer.”
If exception approved: badge “Exception approved (expires <date>)” + helper: “This change can be applied until the exception expires.”
If exception denied: badge “Exception denied” + helper: “Apply is blocked. Update the config diff or rerun evaluation with changes.”

Dylan Brooks: looks good. Two nits:
1) “regresses quality” might be jargon-y. Can we say “reduces output quality”? 
2) For denied, we should also keep “Contact support / #help” link for internal beta.

Alicia Perez: +1 on “reduces output quality”. Also make sure we don’t promise causality (“this change reduces…”) when it could be flaky; maybe “may reduce”?

Aditya Rao: careful: if we say “may reduce” it undermines the gate. We already handle flake with reruns + “inconclusive” state later. For now, failure = deterministic enough to say it does.

Jordan Lee: agree. We can say “was measured to reduce output quality” (keeps it factual).

Kenji Nakamura: updated wording:
Subtext: “This optimization is blocked because it was measured to reduce output quality beyond the allowed threshold.”
Denied helper: “Apply is blocked. Adjust the change or rerun evaluation. If you believe this is incorrect, request a rerun or contact #help.”

Chloe Martin: cool. I’ll make sure Console API returns both gate_status + exception_status so the UI can show “Gate: Failed” + “Exception: Approved” simultaneously.

Felix Schneider: can we also standardize the short pill text for tables?
- Gate: Passed / Failed / Running
- Exception: None / Requested / Approved / Denied
(no extra words)

Dylan Brooks: yes. let’s do that. Kenji can you drop this into DES-611 as the agreed copy + label system? I’ll update ENG-3925 acceptance criteria.

Kenji Nakamura: will do. :thumbsup:

Alicia Perez: :thumbsup:

Aditya Rao: :thumbsup: (and please keep “override” term in audit log + policy docs; UI can say exception)

Dylan Brooks: settled: UI = “exception”, header says “Quality gate …”, always show gate result separately from exception state. Thanks all.
